The checker now recognizes schema-2 state and workflow-supported messages, but it validates a shallow fabricated state rather than workflowctl state invariants and accepts role routes forbidden by the approved design. Its own positive matrix includes User+Main for Deferred-to-Draft and Requirements+Main for In-Progress-to-Deferred.

Basic missing, malformed and unsynchronized reopen evidence now fails, but the latest Superseded record is not bound to the immutable Accepted-to-Draft decision. A later synchronized Draft commit can append a replacement Superseded row and authority bundle while retaining aggregate PASS.
Validated pagination, page-boundary, count, duplicate and digest logic remains present, and all 100/101 boundary cases remain green.
The refreshed 157-case harness retains and passes every cycle-two regression at the exact current head.
The refreshed 157-case harness retains and passes every original governance and error-output regression at the exact current head.

findings.title: Structured credential variants still bypass authorization-grade scanning
findings.observation: The checker normalizes ordinary singular sensitive keys but does not recursively parse flow-style nested objects and matches singular suffixes rather than plural credential containers. A synthetic public.vendor.api.key embedded in a flow-style object and a public.vendor.apiKeys container both return exit 0, SECRETS PASS and aggregate PASS.
findings.trigger: A credential is committed in a flow-style nested object or beneath a plural container such as apiKeys.
findings.impact: A real API key or similar credential can be committed while the authorization-grade result reports PASS.

evidence.description: The tracked contract requires fail-closed scanning at arbitrary public/vendor prefix depth across scalar, array, object and multiline values.
The flow-style nested-key fixture passes unexpectedly; output SHA-256 is dbf1d4624c5f4f05f814d665229805f593295cc2f83ae931e64e25eb8946cc86.
The independent plural apiKeys fixture passes unexpectedly; output SHA-256 is 705caf62882f9e3ec0877eeea661a41e55c8c2e8010d47d9e3b35e33023f5ade.

findings.remediation: Parse every supported structured-text form recursively or conservatively fail closed, normalize singular and plural sensitive containers, keep diagnostics redacted, and add both exact fixtures to the stock harness.
findings.verification: At a new exact head, retain deterministic positive evidence while flow-style nested objects, singular paths, plural credential containers and every prior structured-secret case fail with redacted diagnostics.

findings.title: Lifecycle positives remain unrepresentable by canonical workflow authority
findings.observation: The stock lifecycle matrix uses shallow hand-authored state that workflowctl rejects, including a state missing updatedAt and incomplete feature/GoalRun invariants. It also codifies authority routes forbidden by the approved design: Deferred-to-Draft passes with User+Main although the design requires Requirements+Main, and In-Progress-to-Deferred passes with Requirements+Main although the design requires User+Main.
findings.trigger: A consumer relies on any advertised positive edge that cannot be produced by workflowctl or uses the registry route rather than the approved role route.
findings.impact: Fabricated transition authority can pass while a canonical workflow state fails, so the public lifecycle contract cannot be trusted or implemented end to end.

evidence.description: The approved transition table defines exact authorities for all sixteen edges, including User+Main for In-Progress-to-Deferred and Requirements+Main for Deferred-to-Draft.
workflowctl rejects the stock matrix state as missing updatedAt, while checker transition artifacts pass; primary evidence SHA-256 is 64efd934bac14e7a1bc64e0e6f2e34e58df3c60586b6eb4555caff0a11e82837.
The exact stock harness reports all 157 outcomes successful despite the noncanonical positive matrix; harness SHA-256 is 87af89c09887427b558c1bf97c5e82ce29912794d7527e7d9478793206a56d9d.

findings.remediation: Validate the full canonical workflowctl state invariants, align every registry route with the approved transition table, and generate each positive state and transition through actual workflowctl operations rather than hand-authored shallow state.
findings.verification: At a new exact head, workflowctl must validate every positive state; every edge must use its exact approved role route, source/target stages and immutable decision lineage; forbidden route swaps and impossible recoveries must fail.

findings.title: Reopened Draft authority remains replaceable after the transition
findings.observation: Continuous validation checks only whether the current bundle and latest Superseded row are internally synchronized; it does not bind them to the immutable Accepted-to-Draft transition decision. After a valid reopen, a later Draft commit can append a second Superseded row, later fabricated decision and synchronized plan/portfolio ChangeRecords while the original immutable decision remains unchanged. The checker returns aggregate PASS.
findings.trigger: A same-status Draft commit replaces the latest Superseded record and authority bundle after a valid Accepted-to-Draft transition.
findings.impact: The durable proof that authorized supersession of an Accepted feature can be rewritten without invalidating the project projection.

evidence.description: The contract requires continuous binding of the new bundle to the old feature, latest Superseded record and replaced Accepted record.
A synchronized replacement Superseded record and fabricated later decision pass; output SHA-256 is 9e8bbf92917d6fd57e2a3aed87e4c7003c508dcc1abcd79327560a6ad30a5b34.
A simpler actor/time mismatch also passes; output SHA-256 is 3a768eccceefb291161f5d6051928631aceac630fc0542871812d0d5f6686d7e.

findings.remediation: Bind every latest Superseded actor, time, reason, submitted commit and status-decision identifier to the original Accepted-to-Draft transition lineage. Reject a new Superseded row for an already superseded Accepted record unless a separately authorized compensating transition explicitly permits it.
findings.verification: At a new exact head, retain the unchanged valid reopen fixture while actor/time mismatches, replacement records, fabricated later decisions and synchronized evidence rewrites all fail.

findings.title: Production canonical-state discovery ignores CODEX_HOME
findings.observation: workflowctl resolves its lifecycle root from CODEX_HOME when set, but the production checker always reads os.userInfo().homedir/.codex. The harness hides this difference by rewriting fixture state into the hard-coded location. Running the unmodified checker against a known-valid Ready fixture with an isolated CODEX_HOME fails canonical-state discovery.
findings.trigger: Codex is configured with a supported non-default CODEX_HOME, including isolated CI or managed installations.
findings.impact: A valid public lifecycle cannot be validated and the authorization-grade checker fails closed for the wrong reason in supported environments.

evidence.description: workflowctl honors CODEX_HOME while the production checker constructs the root from the OS home directory.

The exact Ready fixture passes in the harness build but the unmodified checker fails with canonical state missing under isolated CODEX_HOME; output SHA-256 is 833ab559f2f1513fe3d8746e05aecca860c02ff2082b9c44ffa3af1c7cfdcc08.

findings.remediation: Resolve the canonical root with the same CODEX_HOME semantics as workflowctl while retaining path-alias and repository-common-dir protections. Exercise the unmodified production checker against workflowctl-generated state under isolated CODEX_HOME.
findings.verification: At a new exact head, standard-home and isolated-CODEX_HOME workflowctl states must produce identical canonical authority results, while repository-controlled overrides and alias attacks remain rejected.
